name: wgmma_overlap
supersedes: protocol-v2.json (h100-r4 is its data run: C1 refuted -- the issuing warpgroup's stream time depends on the stream's operand form, not one floor; C2 refuted -- L depends on form / G; park control 0: the co-resident chain slowdown is caused by the in-flight ops, not by a parked warp)
question: h100-r4 ($A/microbench/wgmma_overlap/h100-r4, model $A/microbench/wgmma_overlap-model/h100-r4/model.json; 328 / 328 kernels through the gate, run-a == run-b) measured the issuing warpgroup's single-warp stream time while 2-8 ops are in flight (cycles per instruction, ctrl 1.0 / 1.5 / 1.0 / 1.0): fadd1 (1 GPR read) 2.03-2.47 ss / 2.59 rs; fmul2 (2 reads, no reuse) 2.03-2.44 ss / 2.54 rs; ilp8n (3 reads, no reuse) 2.98-3.00 at n256, 3.38-3.44 at n128, 3.88 at n64 / 3.59 rs; ilp8 (3 reads, 2 reuse-served) 3.48-3.87 ss / 4.13 rs. Dependent chains (stall 4) of the issuing warpgroup do not move; chains of a co-resident warpgroup move by +0.1 (G 2) to +0.6 (G 8) at n256 and up to +2.6 (fmnmx) at n64 (G 8); the park control is 0.00-0.09. The stream pattern is read-count shaped: about 2 cycles for 1- or 2-read instructions and about 3 for 3-read ones, with the reuse-flagged 3-read stream slowest. v3 declares the two-part rule that pattern suggests and measures it on a fresh run.

engine_rules_declared_before_data.C3 (issuing warpgroup: half-rate issue +: While a warpgroup has >= 1 wgmma op in flight (issued by any of its warps, not yet complete), for the warps of that warpgroup: (a) a warp's next instruction issues no earlier than 2 cycles after its previous one (control floor = issue + 2, max with the control-word stall and the other floors); (b) the SMSP operand collector serves their general-purpose register reads at one per cycle and the reuse cache does not serve them (every distinct GPR source counts, 64-bit pairs count 2; uniform registers, predicates, immediates, constants, RZ do not count); the OP2p packing rule is otherwise unchanged. Closed-form single-warp prediction: t = max(t_ctrl, 2, n) with n = distinct GPR sources: fadd1 2, fmul2 2, ilp8n 3, ilp8 3, dependent chains (stall 4, n <= 3) unchanged. Other warpgroups on the SM are not affected by (a) / (b).
engine_rules_declared_before_data.C4 (co-resident dependent latency): While >= 1 wgmma op is in flight on the SM, the dependent (scoreboard / fixed-latency) issue of warps NOT in the issuing warpgroup is delayed by L = 0.5 cycle (implemented as a floor alternating 0 / 1 per issue, i.e. the warp's dependent instructions issue at +1 every second time). r4 values at the kernel-relevant in-flight depth (G 8, n256 ss / rs / QGMMA): dep3r 0.58 / 0.48, dep2 0.45, fmnmx 0.64 / 0.56, imad 0.41 / 0.84. Prediction: other.w2 chains t_ctrl + 0.5; park and streams unchanged. Recorded, not installed, if the n128 / n64 cells (r4: 0.8-2.6) are outside tolerance -- the rule is then known to under-predict small-N ops and a later protocol owns the N dependence.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.dropped: single floor F (C1: refuted by the read-count pattern), SM-scope floors and read-port rules (v1).

probe: overlap_v2.cu unchanged (V2=1; same cells, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs); sass_check_v2.py unchanged; derivation of T / e / usable / two-run acceptance as v2.

decision.tolerance: max(15 %, 0.5 cycles per instruction) on gating cells (declared before the run: the collector / issue-slot granularity of the rule is one cycle, and r4's cells spread 0.4 within a kind across N and G, which the rule does not model); secondary cells 25 % or 0.75.
decision.C3 gating cells: self.w1 streams (ilp8, ilp8n, fadd1, fmul2) of the ss forms n256 (G 2 / 4 / 8), n128 (G 4 / 8), n64 (G 8), plus other.w2 streams of every form (must stay within tolerance of ctrl: scope) and self.w1 chains of every form (must stay within tolerance of ctrl: floor is max, not additive).
decision.C3 install: measured if every gating cell is within tolerance and passes the two-run rule; experimental if at least 80 % of the gating cells are within tolerance, no gating cell deviates by more than 1.0 cycle, and the failing cells are listed in the source record; otherwise not installed (recorded).
decision.C3 rs / QGMMA: self.w1 streams of hgmma_bf16_n256_rs and qgmma_e4m3_n256_ss are reported against the same predictions; C3 has no shape parameter, so they do not gate; their residual is recorded in the source (r4: rs +0.5-1.1 above ss).
decision.C4 gating cells: other.w2 chains (dep3r, dep2, fmnmx, imad) of every form and G; park.w2 chains must be within tolerance of ctrl. C4 installed (measured / experimental by the same 100 % / 80 % rule) only if the n256 cells pass; the n128 / n64 cells decide measured vs experimental.
decision.C0: only if every stream and chain gating excess is within tolerance of 0.

install.C3: hopper.wgmma.register_file_issue_steal re-declared as a per-warpgroup in-flight rule (schema timing_row kept: `cycles` = 2 = the issue floor; `enabled` 1; doc field states (a) and (b)); the legacy discrete per-launch table and its three predecessor sources are replaced (quoted in the new source wgmma_overlap.h100.r5). Engine: HopperModule keeps per-warp in-flight op counts through the kWgmma async-group lane (pending ops > 0); Simulator gets an ArchitectureModule query `issue_steal(warp) -> bool`; while true for a warp: control floor issue + cycles after each issue (a), and in the operand collector commit / ready path the warp's instruction takes n_distinct_sources slots at one slot per cycle with reuse_served ignored (b) -- a per-SMSP collector cycle whose read budget is 1 for that instruction. CTest fixtures: (a) one warpgroup, 1-read stream during in-flight ops -> 2 per instruction; (b) 3-read stream -> 3; (c) reuse-served 3-read stream -> 3; (d) stall-4 chain -> 4; (e) after completion -> ctrl values; (f) another warpgroup's stream on the same SM -> unchanged.
install.C4: field `coresident_dependent_half_cycles` (0 / 1) on the same mechanism; engine adds a 0 / 1 alternating floor to register_retry for dependent issues of non-issuing warps while any op is in flight on the SM. Fixture: co-resident dep chain -> 4.5 average.
install.after install: tree build && tree validate --strict; CTest + pytest in a CPU pod; 500 x 2 A/B against mr51 (hp expected to move toward the acc53-k2 arm; bw unchanged); report row, status, docs/en/microbench.md.

record_only: issue-phase durations (r4 table: the issuing warpgroup spends 29-35 cycles per n256 op at W = 1 and 45 at W = 2)
N / G dependence of the stream times beyond C3
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold, candidate or derivation change after data; the diagnostic arm k = 2 is not evidence.
